daily_brief: European Union leaders concluded a tense 12-hour summit in Brussels without agreement on the bloc's 2028-2034 budget, with negotiations set to resume in December amid deep divisions over spending priorities and Ukraine aid [BBC], [RFI]. The impasse comes as Ukraine braces for another difficult winter, with President Zelensky sharply criticizing President Trump's characterization of Vladimir Putin as 'my friend,' comparing it to befriending Hitler during World War Two [BBC]. In Spain, voters head to the polls Sunday in an election dominated by housing affordability protests, with polls suggesting the conservative People's Party will form a government with far-right Vox—potentially the first time the far right enters national government since Franco's dictatorship [BBC]. A significant cybersecurity breach at the U.S. Air Force's Cloud One platform has compromised systems managing sensitive tactical, personnel, and logistics data across hundreds of locations worldwide [The Hindu]. Meanwhile, the UN's food agencies warned that hunger will worsen in 16 countries over the next six months, with Sudan, Yemen, South Sudan, Somalia, and northern Nigeria facing the gravest risks as conflict, fuel costs, and aid cuts converge [Globe and Mail].

top_stories.headline: EU Budget Talks Collapse as Member States Clash Over Spending and Ukraine Aid
bullets: EU leaders ended 12 hours of negotiations in Brussels without agreement on the 2028-2034 budget, with talks postponed until December 17-18
A group of net-contributor countries including Germany, Netherlands, Austria, and Sweden opposed higher spending proposals favored by France and Italy
Germany's Chancellor Merz insisted that Ukraine aid of €45 billion must have unanimous EU support, while Slovakia, Czech Republic, and Hungary objected to the loan
European Council President Antonio Costa's proposal to cut €204 billion from the budget and introduce a digital tax failed to bridge divisions

sources.name: BBC Europe
sources.framing_note: Emphasized the walkout by some members and the pressure to reach agreement before 2027 elections

sources.name: RFI English
sources.framing_note: Highlighted the 'Sensible Seven' coalition and France's deadline concerns ahead of Macron's departure

top_stories.headline: Zelensky Condemns Trump-Putin 'Friendship' as Ukraine Peace Talks Stall
bullets: Ukrainian President Zelensky criticized Trump for calling Putin 'my friend' and posting a photo embracing the Russian leader, calling Putin 'an aggressor and a killer'
Zelensky compared the relationship to befriending Hitler during World War Two, marking his sharpest public criticism of Trump since their 2025 Oval Office meeting
Peace talks mediated in Abu Dhabi earlier this month made no progress; Zelensky said 'the more we know, the more problems'
Trump's envoys have been seen as more aligned with Moscow's positions than Kyiv's; talks are expected to resume in December

sources.name: BBC Europe
sources.framing_note: Led with Zelensky's frustration and included context about delays in US missile deliveries costing Ukrainian lives

sources.name: France 24
sources.framing_note: Brief video coverage focusing on Ukrainians bracing for winter hardships

sources.name: Le Monde
sources.framing_note: Opinion piece framing focused on 'naming the butcher' to stop Ukraine's slaughter

top_stories.headline: Spain Heads to Polls Sunday with Far-Right Poised to Enter Government
bullets: Spanish voters go to ballot boxes Sunday with polls showing Socialist PM Pedro Sánchez likely to lose power after eight years
Conservative People's Party (PP) is projected to win and form a government with far-right Vox party
If Vox enters government, it would be the first time the far right holds national power in Spain's 50 years of post-Franco democracy
Housing affordability has dominated the campaign, with protesters jangling house keys across the country; PP leader pledged to build one million new homes

sources.name: BBC Europe
sources.framing_note: Emphasized the housing crisis as campaign's defining issue and historical significance of potential Vox participation

sources.name: BBC World
sources.framing_note: Included video interviews with young voters describing housing as 'impossible'

top_stories.headline: Hackers Breach U.S. Air Force Cloud One Computing Platform
bullets: Hackers breached the U.S. Air Force's flagship Cloud One cloud computing platform, discovered during system upgrades within the past month
Cloud One manages sensitive applications including air defense radar data, personnel records, pay systems, and munitions tracking across 200+ locations worldwide
The platform combines resources from Microsoft, Amazon, Oracle, and Alphabet; SAIC was the prime contractor
The Air Force declined to comment on specifics; the identity of hackers and scope of data theft remain unknown

sources.name: The Hindu
sources.framing_note: Detailed technical explanation of Cloud One's scope and the systems potentially compromised

top_stories.headline: UN Warns Hunger Crisis to Worsen in 16 Countries as Conflicts and Aid Cuts Collide
bullets: UN food agencies report hunger will worsen in 16 countries over the next six months, with Sudan, Yemen, South Sudan, Somalia, and northern Nigeria at highest risk
In Sudan, nearly 19.5 million people (41% of population) face crisis-level hunger; famine risk persists in 13 areas through January
Sorghum and diesel prices in Sudan have more than doubled due to fighting and Middle East-linked fuel cost increases
Gaza was downgraded one level following the October 2025 ceasefire, though 67% of the population still faces crisis-level hunger or worse

sources.name: Globe and Mail
sources.framing_note: Emphasized the intersection of conflict, fuel costs, and aid cuts driving the crisis
